actual_scope: Audit the unchanged selected PR1087 invoice_allcold.run() input boundary using 54 real-file mutations, then classify invoice survivors through actual assembly, selected upstream controller calls, and one isolated final-binding assertion.
scope_change_reason: Refines the current supplier-boundary card to the exact invoice handoff in Josie Elliston PR1959. The historical owner audit is an orientation control, not a new current bug. The result is finite input-boundary evidence and a conditional implication among five finite guards.
bottleneck_link: Reliability side result with no kappa change: distinguish the invoice producer's finite gates from controller/assembly/source-pin obligations, avoiding a false complete-chain bug claim.
stop_rule: Stop after a consequential accepted invoice case is classified at the actual relevant caller boundary and the bounded prefix/row/logical/halving cases reproduce; report remaining local-provider and all-size obligations.
evidence: 54 cases: invoice rejects 28 and accepts 26; actual assembly rejects 16 of those and accepts 10. Four changed templates accepted by both are rejected upstream; two control-run receipt changes are rejected by the isolated original driver assertion; two are unread controller metadata; two are conservative retained allowances excluded from the selected source by its existing pin. Tight finite boundary pairs and exact integer bounds establish the stated conditional five-guard implication. Honest invoice and assembly reproduce archived evidence.
